assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only the subject's one curated REVIEWED item at basis_commit, read in full with its front matter: the canonical V2 character monograph SHINEPOST_V2_HOTARU_E01_E12_CHARACTER_MONOGRAPH.md (SPV2-CH-HOTARU, version 0.2, 17,700 bytes), a retrospective portrait of the Japanese television anime E01-E12 through the final Brightest office decision, located by observation, claim and adjudication IDs (SPV2-OBS, SPV2-CLM, SPV2-ADJ) and by seconds into each episode. Its author read the accepted episode records with the whole season available and did no new viewing or listening; the listening judgments cited are those of the named source adjudications. The monograph binds the performer Hotaru (松口螢) and Naoki's caller Kei (ケイ) as one person through E12 and keeps SPV2-CH-KEI as a route to the early encounters. The episode readings, ledgers, adjudications and other monographs it links are not curated on this subject, and no claim rests on them. No primary source, performed voice, sung lyric or supplementary material was inspected.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: Two located periods. (1) The 2018 Budokan concert and the after-show meeting with Haru in the empty hall, shown in E01, E04, E06, E08, E09, E11 and E12 recollections and flashbacks (the meeting itself E12, about 469-765 s). (2) The 2022 story present, E01-E12 in episode order, in which she is mostly a voice on Naoki's phone: the E01 dispute over his leaving his earlier work, the E02-E04 requests after he accepts the provisional and then the full Brightest post, the E05 single, the E07 and E10 roll-cake errand, the E10 and E11 calls about her new song and lyrics, and her E12 attendance at Nakano. Her own memory of meeting Haru in 2018 belongs to her at every 2022 state. That Haru is the promising girl Naoki manages is evidenced in her own words from E11 (she calls Haru a promising discovery); the monograph does not place her knowledge of it earlier. The Hotaru/Kei identity is a late disclosure to the viewer (E12), not a change in what she knows. The interval between 2018 and 2022 is unshown.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit, applying the owner calibration rulings recorded there (B/C boundary, single counting of uncertainty, dialogue constrained-use test, chronology splits, relationship-transfer safeguards and control-state attribution); evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The monograph names located wants and one discriminating distinction: she wants Naoki's company and an invitation, not only his services (the objection, once he takes the full Brightest job, that he did not invite her, E02-E04; the E10 response showing that a delivered roll cake did not satisfy a request for his company); she seeks a personal privilege and accepts a professional boundary (special admission to a regular performance refused and his promise of a different occasion accepted, E02-E04); she can see promise in a stranger without deciding for her (E12, 金の卵, no test, offer or enrollment); and she likes an auditorium after the audience has gone because the seats still hold something of the people (E12, her one first-person account). Not B: the monograph leaves open whether the E01 appeal is hurt or a calculated attempt to change his mind, says her threat to give up her activity gives no certain account of what she would have done, and says much more is known about spectators' experience of her than about her own experience of performing. Not D: the wants are located by episode and second, and the privilege-versus-boundary distinction supports narrow extrapolation.

The 2022 calls are in episode order with reasons for each shift in what she asks of Naoki: objection to his leaving (E01), wanting him back when he takes the provisional post, then a call and 'do the work properly' when he refuses, and objection that he did not invite her when he takes the full job (E02-E04), a request to write for her single that he answers by citing his position (E05), interest in seeing the girls and confidence that his work reaches people (E10), and a charge to support the five with the old penalty in reserve after Nakano (E12). The 2018 meeting is located separately. Not B: the change traced is in the relation and in what she asks, not in her own development; the 2018-2022 interval is blank, and her E10 ギリギリ leaves the state of her deadline open. Not D: the states are episode-located with stated causes.

A few attested Japanese forms with their addressees: ナオ for Naoki and his けい/ほたる for her (E12, about 669-670 and 964 s); the mock 切腹 sentence, which the monograph says is an established privilege with Naoki and would have very little basis in a prospective fan's mouth (E01-E12); 道標 and 輝くしるべ and 金の卵 to Haru (E12); the spoken public invitation さあ、輝こう！ (E06 recollection); ギリギリ about her song (E10). The monograph distinguishes three registers by addressee: a public invitation to an audience, mock authority with Naoki, and questions and listening with a lone child. Not C: the forms are few, the row claims no SPEECH, no performed voice was newly heard, and the sung lyric's speaker is not evidence about her in private. Not E: register is analyzed by addressee with a located countercase.

Located ordinary acts: a lunch invitation when Naoki has already eaten (E01), the Kantendō roll-cake errand that she uses as a reason for him to visit, with the listing, order and sending located (E07, E10), a failed ticket purchase and a revived request for a seat (E11), attending Nakano in a cap and leaving without a backstage meeting (E12), and lingering in an empty hall (E12). Not C: ordinary life outside her calls to Naoki and two venue scenes is unseen, and the monograph refuses to infer a favorite food, how much she ate or whether a photograph was taken. Not E: the errand-as-means-to-company pattern recurs across episodes with an outcome.

Three located stances with reasons: with an audience, a public invitation to shine (E01 concert, E06 recollection); with Naoki, the older friend's privilege of absurd penalties, requests for invitations and company, and acceptance of his professional refusals (E01-E12); with Haru alone in 2018, questions about her experience, a volunteered word, and listening long enough for her to find her own words (E12). Spectators' accounts (Kyoka, Rio, Yukine, Ren, Homare, Momiji) are explicitly not evidence of any personal response from her. Not B: only Naoki is sampled at length, Haru in one scene and the audience only as a mass; whether sibling language and childhood intimacy carry more than friendship is left unsettled; her agency, colleagues and other idols are unsampled. Not D: the differences are located and the monograph says why each register fits its addressee.

Located inner states are few: her first-person account of liking the empty hall (E12), real hurt beside a possibly calculated appeal in the E01 dispute, being disconcerted by Naoki's question about her own unfinished lyrics (E11), and her E12 statement that she thinks she can write good lyrics. Not C: the monograph says her internal experience of singing to an audience is not known, and her private circumstances are undisclosed. Not E: these are her own states in distinct, located scenes.

A located repertoire within one relationship: a serious objection that leaving can hurt people too, invoking an older brother's obligations, a threat to give up her activity and 'is this the end' (E01); a renewed objection when he takes the full job (E02-E04); the mock seppuku sentence for small failures (an unanswered call, a ticket, a refused errand, an awkward question); acceptance of a refused special admission and his promise of another occasion (E02-E04); a charge with the penalty in reserve (E12). The monograph distinguishes the serious occasions from the joke. Not B: the conflict sample is Naoki alone, and whether she would carry out the E01 threat is open by the monograph's own account. Not D: the forms recur with located outcomes and an explained distinction.

The row claims no ETHICS. One located value statement: her E01 objection that leaving can hurt people too, which the monograph reads as real hurt alongside an appeal that may be calculated. Returning Haru's bag and asking for privacy (E12) are located acts without stated reasons. Not D: no weighing of alternatives is shown, and the one stated principle cannot be separated from persuasion.

Play is analyzed as a pattern with a function: the extravagant 切腹 sentence recurs for a missed lunch, an unanswered call, a ticket, a refused errand and an awkward question; the monograph calls it an established privilege between two people who know how to answer each other, and says the wit often lies in stating an absurd consequence and waiting for him to discover the practicable thing she wants (E01-E12). The E12 parting allusion to the old penalty extends it. Not B: the play is sampled only with Naoki, and the monograph says it would have little basis with a prospective fan. Not D: the joke and its function recur across episodes with located outcomes.

One dedicated, separately reviewed portrait over the whole E01-E12 season, located to observation IDs and seconds, with adjudicated listening judgments for the contested points (the E01/E11 performance comparison, E10 ギリギリ, the E12 address forms and 輝くしるべ). Not B: it is a compact retrospective portrait over a sparse presence, mostly phone audio with no image of her; its author did no new viewing or listening; and the ledgers and readings it rests on are not curated on this subject. Not D: it is dedicated, reviewed and located.

Affirmative located limits and refused readings: she did not test, recruit or enroll Haru, and Haru's career rests on others' decisions (E12); the lyric's lover and powers are not evidence about her in private (E01); spectators' encounters establish no personal response from her (E04-E12); Rio's E06 recollection replays no identifiable sung Hotaru syllable; Naoki's 'shining' remark over the phone gives him no view of her face; a delivered cake does not satisfy a request for company (E10); there is no completed lyric, title, recipient or transfer (E12); romance, private circumstances and favorite foods stay undisclosed; and the identity binding is not rested on any one weak cue. Not A: the evidence does not explain the gaps it marks. Not C: these are located findings, not inferences from silence.

Claims are placed by episode and seconds; the 2018 concert and meeting are kept separate from the 2022 present; the monograph tracks what the viewer could know when (E01 display name, E11 casting, E12 binding) apart from what she knows; and ambiguous time states are marked (E10 ギリギリ). Not A: the 2018-2022 interval is blank, and when she first learned that Haru was in Naoki's group is not placed before E11. Not C: the placements are precise and the knowledge boundaries explicit.

conditions: Short illustrative lines only, never quotation, in one of the three attested registers: with Naoki, ナオ, requests for an invitation or company, and the mock 切腹 sentence for a small failure; with a lone young fan, questions about what she saw and space to answer; with an audience, a public invitation to shine.
Never give the penalty joke or Naoki's intimacy to a stranger or fan.
No sung lyric text, no new lyric attributed to her, and no performed pitch or delivery.
scenario_readiness.note: The evidence constrains register by addressee with a located countercase and a few attested forms. Not READY: the row claims no SPEECH, the forms are few, and voice was not newly heard. Not NOT_READY: the addressee distinctions are explicit enough to constrain short lines for the declared use.

conditions: The monograph's own counterfactual: after Nakano, another young audience member returns for a lost item. With time and privacy, moderate support for asking what the child saw and letting the child speak; a practical thank-you and prompt departure if the visitor wants only the object. The single strong precedent depends on what Haru volunteered.

An invitation from Naoki: separate a chance to see a performance, see him and stimulate unfinished writing (repeated support) from agreeing to appear publicly on someone else's terms (little support).

A personal request to Naoki that he refuses on professional grounds: predict acceptance of a promised other occasion, not escalation; a departure that threatens their contact (as in E01) is a serious occasion whose outcome stays an open fork.
Include her indirection and overreach: an absurd penalty in place of a plain request, a delivery request that is really a request for his company, and pressing for an invitation over months.
Transfer to an unsampled old friend is a separate, lower-confidence condition; transfer of the Naoki register to anyone else is not supported.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: The 2022 present after E12's Nakano performance, with her 2018 meeting with Haru and her E01-E12 calls with Naoki known to her; or a source-near variant of one located 2022 call that states the changed element. No later career events, no completed lyric and no state inside the unshown 2018-2022 interval.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Naoki (Nao) as her childhood friend and older-brother figure, now Brightest's manager; Haru as the girl she met in 2018 and later recognizes as his idol; a young audience member returning for a lost item, per the monograph. Her agency, colleagues, other idols, family and any romantic partner are unsampled.
setting_constraints: A phone call with Naoki, an empty hall or venue after a show, or attendance at a small Brightest performance as at Nakano.
No rehearsal teaching, contract negotiation, bullying from a stranger or romantic relationship, which the monograph places beyond what has been seen; no cross-series setting.

scenario_readiness.note: Narrow, bounded extrapolation that the monograph itself scopes. Not READY: the stranger case rests on one strong precedent, and what decides the serious E01-type dispute is open. Not NOT_READY: the monograph states supported and unsupported branches with reasons.

conditions: Calls and errands with Naoki: invitations to lunch, requests that turn an errand or ticket into a chance to see him, mock penalties for small failures, and acceptance of a practical substitute with the request for company left standing.
A lone young fan: questions, a volunteered word, a request for privacy and an unceremonious departure.
Food, leisure and private life beyond these: the monograph refuses favorite-food and private-circumstance inferences.
scenario_readiness.note: Ordinary contact is located across episodes. Not READY: it is almost all phone calls with one friend, and her life outside them is unseen. Not NOT_READY: the errand pattern and its outcome recur.

The row claims no ETHICS. The one stated principle (leaving can hurt people too, E01) is read by the monograph as hurt alongside a possibly calculated appeal, and her threat gives no certain account of what she would have done. Nothing supports extrapolating her moral reasoning.

The monograph bounds this affirmatively: her private circumstances, romantic history and attraction remain undisclosed, sibling language and childhood intimacy do not settle those questions, and sustaining a romantic relationship lies beyond what has been seen. Her wish for Naoki's company is covered under MUNDANE_SOCIAL.

conditions: Supported: asking Naoki to write for her single, which he answers by citing his position at Brightest; a request, not a credit or an agreement (E05); a new song under an ambiguous deadline and a stated need for stimulus (E10); a lyric that may emerge from what she receives as an audience member, with no completed text, title or recipient (E11-E12); holding attention on stage as spectators report it (E01, E06, E11).
Not supported: rehearsal teaching, contract negotiation, agency dealings, agreeing to appear publicly on someone else's terms, or delivering a lyric to a named person by a date.
scenario_readiness.note: Her career is located through requests and spectators' accounts. Not READY: her experience of performing is unknown and no professional outcome of her own is shown. Not NOT_READY: the requests, refusals and the unfinished lyric are located with outcomes.

known_limits.statement: The monograph reads the E01 dispute as real hurt alongside an appeal that may be calculated to change Naoki's mind, and says her threat to give up her activity gives no certain account of what she would have done. A model must give an open fork there.
Much more is known about what spectators experienced in discovering her than about her internal experience of singing to them; her liking for the empty hall is the one first-person exception.
The sung lyric's lover and extraordinary powers have no standing as evidence about her in private, and Rio's E06 recollection establishes no identifiable sung Hotaru syllable.
Most of her 2022 presence is Naoki's phone: the picture supplies no image of the remote speaker, so his remark that she is shining is familiar teasing, not observation.
The mock 切腹 sentence is an established privilege with Naoki; the monograph says it would have very little basis in a prospective fan's mouth.
The stranger-child behavior rests on one strong precedent that depended on what Haru volunteered; she did not test, recruit or enroll Haru, and Haru's career rests on others' decisions.
Her private circumstances, romantic history and attraction are undisclosed, and the roll cake and missed lunch give no dependable account of a favorite food.
The precise legal status and reading of every form of her name remain open; the identity binding of Hotaru and Kei rests on the E12 scenes taken together, not on any single cue.
The portrait's author did no new viewing or listening, and the ledgers, readings and adjudications it rests on are not curated on this subject.
Her agency, colleagues, other idols, family and the 2018-2022 interval are unsampled.
